# Rendering Text

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Rendering Text

Every game needs a way to show the score. In Brick Breaker, that means drawing text directly onto the canvas.

Canvas gives you fillText for this. It works just like fillRect but for text. You also get two properties to control how it looks. font for the size and typeface, and textAlign for where the text anchors.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3ctx.font = "18px Arial";
4ctx.fillText("Score: 0", 10, 25);
5ctx.textAlign = "center";
6ctx.fillText("Level 1", 200, 290);
```

Here, "Score: 0" is drawn at (10, 25) - left-aligned by default near the top-left corner. Setting textAlign to "center" then draws "Level 1" horizontally centered at x=200, near the bottom. Note that the y coordinate in fillText is the baseline of the text, not the top edge - so y=25 means the bottom of the letters sits at y=25.

The font property string order matters: "size family" (e.g. "18px Arial"). Writing it in any other order - like "Arial 18px" - silently fails and reverts to the browser default font. I always double-check this when the text looks unexpectedly different from what I set.

![Canvas showing text aligned left, center, and right with coordinate markers](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)
